hero.headline: Two Palm Beach County women arrested in human trafficking operation out of Lake Worth Beach home
hero.teaser: Diana Chaparro Contreras and Sandra Peralta Aguilar are accused of luring a California woman to Florida with a fake job offer and forcing her into prostitution.
hero.body:
Diana Chaparro Contreras, 33, and Sandra Peralta Aguilar, 50, face multiple charges including human trafficking and profiting from arranging prostitution. Both women are currently being held in the Palm Beach County Jail following an investigation into illegal operations at a Lake Worth Beach residence.

The case originated in January when a California woman responded to a housekeeping job posting on Indeed. She was offered $35 per hour and accepted an offer to relocate to Florida with airfare provided. Upon arriving at the home on S. M Street in Lake Worth Beach, her identification documents were confiscated. The victim reported that her passport, Social Security card, and work permit were taken and kept from her. She told investigators she was threatened with deportation and coerced into sexual activity with men who visited the property. The victim was confined to a room with boarded windows and claimed she was forced to have sexual contact with seven men before escaping. She used a lamp to break through plywood covering the window to get out. The victim also reported seeing what may have been a 15-year-old girl present at the location.

During the extended investigation, law enforcement observed numerous men entering and leaving the residence. In April, investigators discovered the operation had relocated to another site less than a mile away. Financial records showed that Chaparro was involved in handling more than $177,000 in cash and bank transactions related to the operation.

Laura Cusack, an advocate with the Human Trafficking Coalition of the Palm Beaches, emphasized that trafficking operations can exist anywhere in the community. "It doesn't just happen in a vacuum or in the underground world. It could happen in the house next door," Cusack said. She stressed that community awareness is vital for identifying these operations. Cusack noted that suspicious activity such as unusual high traffic patterns can be warning signs. She called on residents to report suspected trafficking to authorities, saying that one report can make a significant difference. "These predators are in our community. They can target our children so it just takes one person to make the call, report what they see and that can make all the difference," Cusack said.

Anyone who suspects human trafficking activity should contact the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office. For additional resources and information, the Human Trafficking Coalition of the Palm Beaches can be reached at 561-267-5783 or htcoalitionpb@gmail.com.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $1.6 billion in vetoes
cards.teaser: Gov.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed Florida's $117.6 billion state budget Monday in Tampa, approving a spending plan that takes effect July 1. DeSantis framed the budget as an example of fiscal restraint, saying it marks the fourth straight year the state has reduced spending after his line-item vetoes. The governor pointed to roughly $18 billion in reserves and continued efforts to pay down state debt, noting that the state's debt has been cut in half and the rainy day fund is flush.

The vetoes totaled roughly $1.6 billion, with about $800 million tied to direct line-item spending. Major reductions came across corrections, water and resiliency projects, education, higher education, local public safety initiatives, and community programs. Florida's prison system saw tens of millions eliminated for repairs, new correctional housing units, capital improvements, and pay adjustments. Water and resiliency projects saw more than $170 million cut, including local stormwater, wastewater, flood mitigation, and infrastructure projects. Education cuts included $15 million for Catholic school security and millions for college infrastructure tied to Palm Beach State College, College of the Florida Keys, Indian River State College, and Florida State University's College of Nursing. House Minority Leader Fentrice Driskell said Democratic projects were vetoed at roughly a two-to-one rate compared to Republican counterparts. DeSantis said this year's vetoes bring his budget cuts over eight years to more than $10 billion, far more than his recent predecessors combined.

cards.headline: House Passes Major Children's Online Safety Bill With Florida Lawmakers Leading Negotiations
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. House of Representatives approved the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act on a 267-117 vote, with Florida's congressional delegation playing a significant role in shaping the legislation. Tampa Democrat Kathy Castor, who had previously led Democratic resistance to earlier versions of the proposal, ultimately backed the revised bill after changes addressed her concerns about holding tech companies accountable for harms linked to their platforms. Palm Harbor Republican Gus Bilirakis, who authored the Kids Online Safety Act, saw his provisions incorporated into the broader package. Bilirakis cited statistics showing nearly half of American teenagers are online almost constantly, with about half spending four or more hours daily on screens for leisure and 95% owning smartphones.

The legislation extends privacy protections to children under 13 for the first time and mandates that technology companies give families greater control over children's online experiences. The bill prohibits targeted advertising directed at minors and preserves state authority to impose additional restrictions beyond federal requirements. Thonotosassa Republican Laurel Lee saw significant elements of her Safe Internet for Minors Act folded into the final measure. The bill did not unite the entire House, with 32 Republicans and 85 Democrats opposing it, including Florida's Jimmy Patronis of Fort Walton Beach, Anna Paulina Luna of St. Petersburg, and Maxwell Frost of Orlando.

cards.headline: Tri-Rail gets $60 million to avoid shutdown, Palm Beach County projects funded in state budget
cards.teaser: Local agencies received over $30 million in state budget funding, including money to keep Tri-Rail operating and infrastructure upgrades across Palm Beach County.
cards.body:
Tri-Rail secured $60 million in Florida's 2026-2027 state budget, ensuring the commuter rail system can continue operating after facing a potential shutdown in July without the funding. Florida State Senator Mack Bernard emphasized the importance of the allocation for residents traveling between Palm Beach County, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties. "Transportation is the key, because I know people are trying to get to work, schools and Tri-Rail plays that major role, between the residents of Palm Beach County, Broward and Dade," Bernard said. Regular rider Stanley Lucien, who commutes from Boca Raton to Miami for business, praised the service's affordability. "It's cheaper it does save you a lot of money," Lucien said. "If I could fund it, I'd fund it myself."

Palm Beach County also achieved significant infrastructure funding through the $117 billion state budget. The county secured $1.5 million for the new Riviera Beach water treatment plant and $2 million for drainage repairs to Australian Avenue from 45th Street to Palm Beach Lakes, which is part of a larger $65 million project. The state approved an additional $3 million for traffic safety improvements on Okeechobee Boulevard. Bernard noted that Palm Beach County received over $30 million in approved funding, representing 75 percent of the total amount requested in the budget. "In all this was a good year for Palm Beach County," Bernard said.

Other local organizations benefited from the budget approval. The Arc of the Palm Beaches in West Palm Beach received $1.5 million for a special needs shelter, while the Boys & Girls Club secured $1.5 million for its Teen Readiness Center. These investments support vulnerable populations and youth development in the region.

However, Governor Ron DeSantis vetoed nearly $1.6 billion in proposed spending, including several Palm Beach County priorities. The governor struck $2 million for water treatment plant expansions, $900,000 for road improvements and beautification in South Bay, $125,000 for Ocean Inlet beach access improvements, and $200,000 for repairs and operations at Delray Beach's historic American Legion building. State Representative Rob Long, who advocated for the American Legion funding, expressed determination to continue pushing for the project during the next budget cycle. The historic building holds significant cultural importance to the community as a hub for Black residents in the area.

cards.headline: Florida state budget cuts hit Indian River State College, Palm Beach State College projects
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis vetoed millions of dollars in college infrastructure and program funding as part of $1.6 billion in budget cuts.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed Florida's $117.6 billion state budget Monday, which takes effect July 1. After line-item vetoes totaling roughly $1.6 billion, DeSantis said the budget marks the fourth straight year Florida has reduced spending. The final budget still funds major priorities including education, transportation, environmental restoration, law enforcement, and tax relief. DeSantis also noted the state has roughly $18 billion in reserves, has cut debt in half, and maintains a flush rainy day fund.

Education vetoes included $15 million for Catholic school security and millions more for college infrastructure and programs, cutting projects at Palm Beach State College, College of the Florida Keys, Indian River State College, and Florida State University's College of Nursing. About $800 million of the $1.6 billion in total vetoes were tied to direct line-item spending, with the remainder spread across corrections, water and resiliency projects, local public safety initiatives, and community programs. House Minority Leader Fentrice Driskell criticized the cuts, arguing Democratic projects were vetoed at roughly twice the rate of Republican projects. DeSantis said this year's vetoes bring his budget cuts over eight years to more than $10 billion.

cards.headline: Singer Island 25-story development proposal raises concerns over world-renowned Blue Heron Bridge reef
cards.body:
A New York-based developer, The Continuum Company, has proposed Singer Island Gateway, an approximately $14 million mixed-use development at 2525 Lake Drive in Palm Beach County. The project would include hundreds of residential units, commercial and public space, and a marina, with the main structure rising 25 stories at the entrance to Singer Island. The location places the development directly above the underwater reef at Phil Foster Park near Blue Heron Bridge, a destination that attracts divers and snorkelers from around the world.

The reef draws visitors for its remarkable marine ecosystem. People who visit the area describe seeing stingrays, rainbow-colored fish, blue and yellow fish, pink coral, yellow coral, and striped fish in the shallow waters. Louis Espinosa, a diver who frequents the location, described it simply as "beautiful, amazing" and called it one of the best spots he has visited. The combination of accessible shallow water and diverse sea life has made this area renowned among diving enthusiasts globally.

However, longtime resident Gary Heiser, who grew up in the area, has expressed serious reservations about the project's scale and placement. He believes the 25-story tower is inappropriate for the location, noting that while such a structure might work in cities like Chicago, it does not fit here. Beyond aesthetic concerns, Heiser worries that construction activities, the shade cast by the tall building, and the marina could harm the marine life below. "I don't think it's a good idea that this treasure gets impacted to such a great extent," he said. An environmental study posted on the developer's website presents a contrasting view. A geoscientist concluded that the development would have no impact on marine life in the Lake Worth Lagoon, with the ecosystem remaining unchanged. Heiser remains skeptical of these findings, stating he would like to see additional research before accepting such conclusions.

Opinions among reef visitors diverge on the matter. While Heiser opposes the project based on potential environmental damage, Espinosa indicated his position depends on whether there is genuine evidence of harm to the reef. "If it doesn't disturb the reef, I don't see a problem with it," Espinosa said. The proposal has not yet been approved. The developer has been contacted for comment, with a response still pending. Meanwhile, residents have launched a petition opposing the Singer Island Gateway project.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis Vetoes $95 Million in South Florida Local Projects From State Budget
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis slashed more than $95 million in South Florida appropriations from the state budget Monday, canceling funds for hundreds of local projects across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis vetoed more than $95 million in South Florida-specific appropriations from Florida's $117.6 billion state budget, canceling funds for hundreds of local projects across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties. The vetoes, detailed in a 39-page line-item letter sent to Secretary of State Cord Byrd, are part of $1.7 billion in total state vetoes DeSantis announced when he signed the budget. Miami-Dade County lost the most at roughly $55.3 million in local appropriations, while Broward lost about $20.7 million and Palm Beach County saw $19.4 million in canceled state funding.

The single largest South Florida veto was $5 million for security funding for Catholic schools in Miami-Dade, sought by Miami Republican Rep. Mike Redondo. DeSantis defended the cut by contrasting it with Florida's school-choice scholarship program, which has shifted public education dollars to Catholic schools and other private institutions. He said he does not want security funding to become "an entitlement" the state would be expected to renew indefinitely. Additional Miami-Dade vetoes included $2 million apiece for water and stormwater projects, including security upgrades for the county's water and sewer infrastructure and a water-main capacity upgrade in Homestead. In Broward County, both of the two largest vetoes were $2 million each: a stormwater mitigation project in Hallandale Beach and a bridge replacement in Lighthouse Point. Palm Beach County's biggest veto was $4.8 million for a remodel of Palm Beach State College's Boca Raton administration building, and DeSantis also struck $3 million for a helicopter purchase for the Health Care District of Palm Beach County's emergency operations.

cards.headline: Diver Greer Boyd of Fort Pierce identified after death near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office identified a Fort Pierce man who died Friday while diving to recover a trolling motor.
cards.body:
Greer Boyd, 63, of Fort Pierce has been identified as the diver found dead Friday near the Fort Pierce Inlet. According to investigators with the Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Boyd was fishing with friends earlier in the day when the boat's trolling motor became detached and went overboard. The group returned to the area with diving equipment to attempt recovery of the motor.

Boyd entered the water alone, and only his buoyancy compensator and air tank were located approximately 40 yards from the boat. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding a missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed four vessels to assist in the search. Martin County Fire Rescue Lt. Daniel DeGrazia, who was off-duty at the time, recovered Boyd's body at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. An autopsy is scheduled.

cards.headline: Two killed in Florida's Turnpike crash in Martin County, fifth traffic fatality in four days
cards.teaser: A crash on Florida's Turnpike near mile marker 132 closed all lanes in both directions for multiple hours Monday afternoon.
cards.body:
A crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County killed two people and shut down all lanes in both directions for multiple hours on Monday afternoon. According to the Martin County Fire Rescue, the wreck happened near mile marker 132 at about 3 p.m. In addition to the two fatalities, firefighter-paramedics transported one person with traumatic injuries by ground to the hospital. The Martin County Sheriff's Office reported that both northbound and southbound lanes were completely shut down at 3:49 p.m., with all lanes reopening at about 8 p.m.

This crash marks the fifth traffic fatality in four days in Martin County, according to the sheriff's office. A Palm City man died overnight following a two-vehicle crash on the Turnpike early Monday morning. Additionally, two people were killed in a head-on crash Saturday morning on Allapattah Road in Indiantown. The cause of the Monday afternoon crash has not been released.

cards.headline: One person dies in Hobe Sound house fire on Southeast Cactus Trail
cards.teaser: Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a house fire Monday afternoon in the 7000 block of Southeast Cactus Trail where one person died.
cards.body:
One person died Monday afternoon in a house fire in Hobe Sound, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. Firefighters responded just after 3 p.m. to a home in the 7000 block of Southeast Cactus Trail. When crews from Martin County Fire Rescue Station 32 arrived, they found heavy smoke coming from all doors and windows of the home. Firefighters entered the house, located an unresponsive person, and removed them from the home.

Paramedics treated the victim and transported them by ambulance to a hospital with life-threatening injuries. Martin County Fire Rescue later confirmed the person died. Stuart Fire Rescue also responded to assist under a mutual aid agreement. The State Fire Marshal has been notified and is investigating the cause of the fire.

cards.headline: Singer Island Gateway 25-story development proposal sparks concern over Blue Heron Bridge reef
cards.teaser: A proposed 25-story waterfront development near Phil Foster Park is raising questions about the impact on a world-renowned reef at the base of Blue Heron Bridge.
cards.body:
The Continuum Company, a New York-based developer, has proposed Singer Island Gateway, an approximately $14 million mixed-use project along 2525 Lake Drive. The plan includes hundreds of residential units, commercial and public space, and a marina near the base of the bridge, rising 25 stories at the entrance to Singer Island in Palm Beach County. The proposal is raising questions about the impact on the underwater ecosystem surrounding Phil Foster Park at the base of Blue Heron Bridge, known for drawing divers and snorkelers from across the globe.

Longtime resident Gary Heiser said the scale and placement of the project are fundamentally incompatible with the location. He worries that construction activity, increased shade from the tower, and the addition of a marina could disrupt the marine life that has made the reef world-renowned. An environmental study published on the developer's website concluded the planned development would have no impact on the marine life in the Lake Worth Lagoon, stating the ecosystem will remain unchanged. Heiser said he finds it hard to believe there would be no impact and would like to see more research. Nothing has been approved yet. Residents have started a petition against the proposal, and the developer has been contacted for comment.

cards.headline: 400-pound black bear killed after being hit by car on Southwest Martin Highway
cards.teaser: A male black bear weighing 400 pounds was killed Monday morning after getting hit by a car on Southwest Martin Highway near Southwest Warfield Boulevard.
cards.body:
A 400-pound male black bear was killed Monday morning after being struck by a car on Southwest Martin Highway near Southwest Warfield Boulevard. According to Major Ruben Romero with the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the driver was not speeding and stopped to wait for deputies to arrive. The driver reported that the bear ran into the roadway before being hit by the vehicle. The driver was not injured, but the bear died at the scene.

The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission removed the bear from the scene. Michael Orlando, bear program coordinator with FWC, said he believes the bear was dispersing, which occurs when bears become old enough to leave their mother and pack to find a new home. Orlando explained that bears will walk 50 to 100 miles in any direction while trying to figure out where they are going. The bear is now with FWC in Collier County, where officials will collect data to determine where it came from. This marks the second bear sighting on the Treasure Coast this month.

cards.headline: Palm City man dies after collision between SUV and semi-truck on Florida's Turnpike
cards.teaser: A 41-year-old man from Palm City died early Monday morning after his Nissan Rogue collided with the back of a semi-truck trailer on the Turnpike in Martin County.
cards.body: A 41-year-old Palm City man died early Monday morning after his Nissan Rogue SUV collided with a semi-truck on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County at mile marker 136. According to Florida Highway Patrol, the Nissan was traveling northbound in the outside lane when it struck the back of the trailer of a semi-truck also in the outside lane. The driver was transported to Florida Coast Medical Center and pronounced deceased at 1:55 a.m. The semi-truck driver was not injured. FHP is investigating the crash.

Major Ruben Romero with the Martin County Sheriff's Office said the driver was not speeding and stopped to wait for deputies. The driver told deputies the bear ran into the roadway before being struck. The driver was not injured, but the bear died at the scene. Romero said it is important for drivers to be aware of wildlife, especially on rural roads during morning or evening hours.

The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission removed the bear from the scene. Michael Orlando, bear program coordinator with FWC, said he believes the bear was dispersing, which occurs when bears get old enough to leave their mother and pack to find a new home. Orlando said they walk 50 to 100 miles in any direction trying to figure out where they are going. The bear is currently with FWC in Collier County, where they will collect data to determine where it came from. This is the second bear sighting on the Treasure Coast this month. A black bear was previously caught on camera swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community of Port St. Lucie.

cards.headline: Woman, 78, killed after SUV rolls backward in Port St. Lucie driveway
cards.teaser: A 78-year-old woman died Sunday morning after a 2016 Lincoln MKX SUV rolled backward and struck her in a residential driveway in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
A 78-year-old woman was killed Sunday morning after a 2016 Lincoln MKX SUV rolled backward and struck her in a residential driveway in Port St. Lucie. The incident occurred at approximately 10:47 a.m. according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The woman was standing outside the vehicle near the open driver's door when the SUV began rolling backward. The open door struck her, knocking her to the ground. Her adult son, 59, was in the passenger seat and had started the vehicle. The cause of the rollback remains under investigation. The woman was transported to Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, where she was pronounced deceased at 11:19 a.m.

Neighbors who knew the woman for several years remembered her for simple acts of kindness. "I saw the ambulance, the fire trucks, and two or three police cars. I felt sad, sad because I've known her for many years," said neighbor Daisy Cardona. "On Sundays, they would bring us bread, cupcakes, donuts, and sometimes cakes that were this big. May she rest in peace and my condolences to her family." The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate the incident.

hero.headline: Fort Myers Mussels defeat St. Lucie Mets in series finale as Fragoza hits two home runs
hero.teaser: The Fort Myers Mussels beat the St. Lucie Mets in the final game of their weekend series, powered by two home runs from Fragoza.
hero.body:
The Fort Myers Mussels secured a victory over the St. Lucie Mets in their series finale, with Fragoza providing the offensive spark by hitting two home runs in the game. The performance highlighted the Mussels' ability to generate runs at a critical moment in the series.

Fragoza's two-homer display proved to be the difference maker in the contest, as his power hitting drove in key runs for the Mussels. The series between these two Florida State League competitors concluded with this weekend matchup, capping off what had been an extended series due to scheduling adjustments earlier in the season.

The St. Lucie Mets, the Single-A affiliate of the New York Mets, play their home games at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. The team had faced the Mussels, who are based in Fort Myers, in this series that required rescheduling due to a postponement that had pushed one contest back to late July. Despite the scheduling complications, both teams were able to complete their series competition.

The Mussels' offense took advantage of their opportunities against the Mets pitching staff in the finale, with Fragoza leading the charge. His two home runs gave Fort Myers the edge they needed to secure the series-ending victory and demonstrate their competitive standing within the league.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets game postponed, rescheduled for late July in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: The St.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets postponed their game against the Fort Myers Mussels on Saturday, with the matchup now rescheduled for late July in Port St. Lucie. The game was originally scheduled to take place at Clover Park.

The Mussels and Mets will complete the series when they meet again later in the season. The specific makeup date in late July has been set but officials have not announced the exact day of the rescheduled contest.

The postponement came before the weekend series finale between the two Florida State League teams. The St. Lucie Mets play their home games at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie.

The Mets are the Single-A affiliate of the New York Mets. Fans who purchased tickets for the postponed game can use them for the rescheduled date or contact the team's ticket office for alternatives.

cards.headline: Jorge Polanco goes hitless in rehab appearance for Syracuse Mets
cards.teaser: New York Mets player Jorge Polanco failed to record a hit during a minor league rehabilitation appearance for Syracuse on Sunday.
cards.body:
Jorge Polanco went hitless during a minor league rehabilitation appearance for the Syracuse Mets on Sunday. The New York Mets player is working his way back from injury through the team's Triple-A affiliate.

Polanco's rehab assignment continues as he attempts to return to the major league roster. The Syracuse Mets are the top minor league affiliate of the New York Mets, one level above the St. Lucie Mets in Port St. Lucie.

The organization uses its minor league system to help injured major league players regain form before returning to active duty. Polanco's performance will determine when he is ready to rejoin the big league club.

hero.headline: SoFlo Market Brings July 4 Celebration to Boca Raton City Hall
hero.teaser: The monthly SoFlo Market will hold a patriotic Independence Day celebration at Boca Raton City Hall on Saturday, July 4, with free admission, food vendors, kids activities and appearances by firefighters and police officers.
hero.body:
SoFlo Market will turn Boca Raton City Hall into a Fourth of July celebration on Saturday, July 4, organizer Tatiana Freitas told WPTV. The free monthly event will run from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. at 201 West Palmetto Park Road, featuring vendors, food, and family activities with patriotic themes. The first 20 children through the gate will receive a free gift.

Activities include a kids parade, face painting, a foggy bubble station, mini golf and balloon twisting. A DJ will provide music, and the SoFlo Market flamingo mascot will make an appearance. Boca Raton firefighters and police officers have been invited to participate in the celebration.

Freitas said the monthly market uplifts small local businesses and brings the community together. Her husband Eddie and son Kyle are part of the organizing team. Generators will provide electricity on-site, and the event will be documented on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube channels throughout the day.

cards.headline: Boca Raton George Snow Scholarship Fund Awards Record $7.5 Million to 470 Students
cards.teaser: The George Snow Scholarship Fund in Boca Raton awarded more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students in Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, marking a record year for the nonprofit.
cards.body:
The George Snow Scholarship Fund, headquartered in Boca Raton, awarded a record $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, President Tim Snow told WPTV. Since its founding over 40 years ago, the nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students, making it the largest scholarship provider in Palm Beach County. The program provides four-year commitments designed to bridge the gap between traditional financial aid and what students and families can afford.

Beyond financial assistance, the fund offers mentorship, professional development and the College Compass podcast, according to Vice President of Development Jay Brandt. One 2026 recipient, Zya Chow, a Wellington Community High School graduate, received both the Royal Palm Hearing Aid Scholarship and the Davidowitz Family Caregiving Youth Scholarship and plans to attend Georgetown University. The Doyle-Whelchel Scholars Boutique, led by Scholar Services Coordinator Garvey Antoine, provides professional, formal and casual clothing to help scholars attend interviews, internships and campus events. The boutique accepts donations of new or gently used clothing, footwear and accessories.

cards.headline: Vero Beach MusicWorks Launches Fourteenth Concert Season
cards.body:
MusicWorks in Vero Beach is launching its fourteenth concert season, expanding cultural tourism and inspiring multi-state travel. The concert series aligns Florida with California, Texas, New York, Tennessee, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, Arizona, Michigan and Massachusetts in drawing visitors for performances.

The season positions Vero Beach as a destination for concert-goers from multiple states seeking cultural events. MusicWorks has built a reputation over more than a decade of seasons, bringing performances to Indian River County.

The concert series contributes to tourism in Vero Beach by attracting visitors who travel specifically for musical performances. The fourteenth season continues the organization's pattern of annual programming that draws audiences beyond Florida.

MusicWorks schedules performances throughout the season at venues in Vero Beach. The series has established itself as part of the cultural landscape in Indian River County over its fourteen-year history.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds Launches $20 Million Statewide Ad Campaign for Governor
hero.teaser: The Friends of Byron Donalds political committee launched two new television and digital ads statewide Tuesday, part of a $20 million buy that represents the largest single media investment of the 2026 gubernatorial race.
hero.body:
Byron Donalds' political committee has unveiled a pair of new television and digital advertisements as part of a sweeping $20 million media investment across Florida. The two spots, titled "Jack Up" and "Shot," are now running on cable and broadcast television as well as streaming platforms throughout the state. This spending represents the largest single media buy of the 2026 gubernatorial race.

In the "Jack Up" advertisement, Donalds positions himself alongside President Donald Trump and Governor Ron DeSantis regarding artificial intelligence data centers in Florida. He pledges to safeguard state ratepayers from potential utility rate increases and environmental damage that could result from AI data center development. The second spot, "Shot," focuses on the affordability challenges confronting Florida families. The ad opens with Donalds sharing a personal story about his mother, who worked two jobs in Brooklyn while still struggling to meet expenses. He describes how his move to Florida nearly three decades ago provided him with the opportunity to build a successful life.

Ryan Smith, who chairs the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee, emphasized that the candidate is committed to reducing costs for Florida residents across different age groups and income levels. According to Smith, the advertisements highlight Donalds' character and his priorities as a potential governor, including achieving lower costs, protecting consumers, and maintaining Florida as a place where people can pursue their ambitions. The media investment demonstrates Donalds' financial strength in the race, as he has consistently broken fundraising records throughout his campaign.

Beyond his advertising push, Donalds has built an extensive ground operation that has made contact with more than 175,000 voters through door-to-door canvassing. His campaign has also assembled significant support from prominent conservative figures and elected officials. He holds endorsements from President Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Elon Musk, Charlie Kirk, U.S. Senator Rick Scott, the majority of Florida's sheriffs, and numerous state legislators and conservative leaders. This combination of financial resources, grassroots organization, and high-profile backing positions Donalds as a dominant force in the Republican primary for the 2026 gubernatorial election.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis Vetoes $95 Million in South Florida Local Projects From State Budget
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis slashed more than $95 million in South Florida appropriations from the state budget Monday, canceling funds for hundreds of local projects across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis vetoed more than $95 million in South Florida-specific appropriations from Florida's $117.6 billion state budget, canceling funds for hundreds of local projects across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties. The vetoes, detailed in a 39-page line-item letter sent to Secretary of State Cord Byrd, are part of $1.7 billion in total state vetoes DeSantis announced when he signed the budget. Miami-Dade County lost the most at roughly $55.3 million in local appropriations, while Broward lost about $20.7 million and Palm Beach County saw $19.4 million in canceled state funding.

The single largest South Florida veto was $5 million for security funding for Catholic schools in Miami-Dade, sought by Miami Republican Rep. Mike Redondo. DeSantis defended the cut by contrasting it with Florida's school-choice scholarship program, which has shifted public education dollars to Catholic schools and other private institutions. He said he does not want security funding to become "an entitlement" the state would be expected to renew indefinitely. Additional Miami-Dade vetoes included $2 million apiece for water and stormwater projects, including security upgrades for the county's water and sewer infrastructure and a water-main capacity upgrade in Homestead. In Broward County, both of the two largest vetoes were $2 million each: a stormwater mitigation project in Hallandale Beach and a bridge replacement in Lighthouse Point. Palm Beach County's biggest veto was $4.8 million for a remodel of Palm Beach State College's Boca Raton administration building, and DeSantis also struck $3 million for a helicopter purchase for the Health Care District of Palm Beach County's emergency operations.

cards.headline: House Passes Major Children's Online Safety Bill With Florida Lawmakers Leading Negotiations
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. House of Representatives approved the Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act on a 267-117 vote, with Florida's congressional delegation playing a significant role in shaping the legislation. Tampa Democrat Kathy Castor, who had previously led Democratic resistance to earlier versions of the proposal, ultimately backed the revised bill after changes addressed her concerns about holding tech companies accountable for harms linked to their platforms. Palm Harbor Republican Gus Bilirakis, who authored the Kids Online Safety Act, saw his provisions incorporated into the broader package. Bilirakis cited statistics showing nearly half of American teenagers are online almost constantly, with about half spending four or more hours daily on screens for leisure and 95% owning smartphones.

The legislation extends privacy protections to children under 13 for the first time and mandates that technology companies give families greater control over children's online experiences. The bill prohibits targeted advertising directed at minors and preserves state authority to impose additional restrictions beyond federal requirements. Thonotosassa Republican Laurel Lee saw significant elements of her Safe Internet for Minors Act folded into the final measure. The bill did not unite the entire House, with 32 Republicans and 85 Democrats opposing it, including Florida's Jimmy Patronis of Fort Walton Beach, Anna Paulina Luna of St. Petersburg, and Maxwell Frost of Orlando.

cards.headline: Civil Liberties Groups Challenge New Florida Laws Set to Take Effect July 1
cards.teaser: More than a hundred new state laws take effect July 1, bringing court challenges against several measures that civil liberties experts say threaten constitutional freedoms.
cards.body:
Civil liberties groups are mounting legal challenges against several Florida laws set to take effect July 1. HB 1471 concentrates power in the hands of a few government officials to label organizations as "domestic terrorist organizations" without adequate due process, transparency, or safeguards against political abuse. Civil liberties experts contend the law violates the First Amendment and threatens to chill protected speech and association. HB 991, taking effect in 2027, makes voter registration and casting ballots harder for Floridians who lack easy access to a new, more restrictive list of citizenship documents. The law affects older voters, low-income voters, naturalized citizens, citizens born at home, and women whose names changed after marriage or divorce. Legal analysts say HB 991 is likely unconstitutional and violates the 14th Amendment's Equal Protection Clause.

The property tax amendment that Gov. Ron DeSantis pushed through in a Special Session also faces legal challenges from local officials, who claim the ballot language is confusing and deceitful. Local officials argue the amendment will result in higher rents, cuts to critical local services, and a shift toward increased taxes and fees. A provision requiring new Florida residents to wait five years to receive the tax break could be deemed unconstitutional. DeSantis' new congressional maps are also in legal limbo, with critics calling them an unconstitutional partisan power grab that violates the Fair Districts Amendments Florida voters passed in 2010.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg Mayor Faces Attack Ad Over 34% City Hall Attendance Record
cards.teaser: A new ad from the political committee St Pete Shines targets Mayor Ken Welch over a Tampa Bay Times report that found he swiped his keycard into City Hall just 34% of workdays.
cards.body:
A new political advertisement from the committee St Pete Shines targets St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch's attendance record at City Hall. The spot centers on a Tampa Bay Times report finding that Welch swiped his keycard into City Hall just 34% of workdays. The ad features real-sounding residents reacting to the statistic, with one saying they would be fired before the end of the week for similar attendance. Creative elements include MISSING posters bearing the Mayor's face on light poles and the number 34% sculpted into hedges, beer foam and bread, each tagged with "the Tampa Bay Times has the receipts." The advertisement ends with the call to action "Fire Ken Welch."

The campaign connects Welch's absences to incomplete projects. The Historic Gas Plant District redevelopment is years behind schedule, with the old police headquarters site at The Central producing little more than a parking garage and deadlines slipping to 2030. The Moffitt cancer campus, which could have anchored thousands of jobs, collapsed during Welch's tenure. Additionally, when residents faced runaway water bills, the Mayor declined to answer questions on camera. The committee's strategy makes the 34% statistic a memorable focal point that other grievances can attach to, giving voters a single number to associate with the Mayor's overall performance.

cards.headline: Manatee County Sheriff Endorses Commissioner Mike Rahn for Re-election
cards.teaser: Manatee County Sheriff Rick Wells endorsed County Commissioner Mike Rahn for re-election, praising the Marine Corps veteran for his support for public safety resources.
cards.body:
Manatee County Sheriff Rick Wells is endorsing County Commissioner Mike Rahn for re-election. Wells praised Rahn as "a Marine Corps veteran, a relentless fighter, and exactly the kind of leader Manatee County needs," noting that since taking office, Rahn has "stood shoulder-to-shoulder with law enforcement, supporting the resources we need to keep families safe." Rahn served 13 years in the U.S. Marine Corps, both on active duty and in the reserves, including service during Operation Desert Storm, and earned multiple meritorious citations before being honorably discharged.

Since joining the County Commission, Rahn has made public safety central to his re-election campaign. His campaign said he voted to fully fund the Manatee County Sheriff's Office and supported installation of about 3,000 new streetlights to improve public safety across the county. Rahn also highlights his support for law enforcement investments, infrastructure, flood protection and transportation, as well as holding the line on taxes and unnecessary spending. Rahn has worked in the residential mortgage industry for more than 29 years in the Manatee-Sarasota market and previously served on the Manatee County Planning Commission. He holds leadership roles with the Manatee-Sarasota Building Industry Association, the Florida Home Builders Association and the National Association of Home Builders, and was elected to the Florida Housing Hall of Fame in 2017. Rahn is running against community advocate Glen Gibellina in the Republican Primary, with write-in candidate Allison Sneed also qualifying.

cards.headline: Florida Executing Prisoners at Record Pace as Most States Move Away From Death Penalty
cards.teaser: Florida is executing prisoners at a record pace, according to ProPublica, while most of the United States continues to abandon the death penalty.
cards.body:
The report published Tuesday highlights Florida's increased use of capital punishment at a time when national trends show declining support for the death penalty. The story examines the pace of executions in Florida compared to other states and the broader national movement away from capital punishment.

Florida's execution rate stands in contrast to trends across much of the country, where states have either abolished the death penalty or significantly reduced its use. The increased pace in Florida represents a departure from the national pattern of declining executions. The full scope of Florida's execution schedule and the factors driving the state's approach were detailed in the ProPublica investigation.

hero.headline: Sebastian Pines Land Use Application Moves to State Review
hero.teaser: A land use proposal for Sebastian Pines has advanced to state review after local approval.
hero.body:
The Sebastian Pines land use application has been forwarded to the state for review. The proposal cleared local hurdles and is now entering the state approval process.

The project involves land use changes for the Sebastian Pines property. State officials will now evaluate the application according to Florida land use regulations.

No timeline has been provided for the state review process. The application must receive state approval before any development can proceed on the Sebastian Pines site.

cards.headline: Vero Premier Properties Launches Luxury Real Estate Firm Focused on Private Network Sales
cards.teaser: Vero Premier Properties has launched in Vero Beach with a business model built around private network sales rather than online portals.
cards.body:
Vero Premier Properties has launched in Vero Beach with a business model built around private network sales rather than online portals. The luxury real estate firm announced its opening Monday.

The company is targeting high-net-worth buyers who typically do not browse public real estate listings. Vero Premier Properties is structured to serve clients who rely on private connections and personal networks to identify and purchase luxury properties.

The firm's approach reflects the way wealthy buyers actually conduct real estate transactions in Vero Beach's luxury market. Rather than competing through traditional online listing platforms, the company is positioning itself as a private broker for exclusive properties.

Vero Premier Properties is now operating in Vero Beach. The company has not disclosed specific office locations or the number of agents on staff.

cards.headline: Indian River Lagoon Restoration Efforts Get New Support
cards.teaser: Conservation groups are working to improve conditions in the Indian River Lagoon.
cards.body:
Friends of the Everglades announced new efforts to restore the Indian River Lagoon. The organization is pursuing initiatives aimed at improving water quality and habitat conditions in the lagoon.

The Indian River Lagoon has faced environmental challenges including pollution and habitat degradation. The new restoration work is part of ongoing efforts to reverse damage to the estuary system.

Friends of the Everglades is coordinating with local and state agencies on the lagoon restoration projects. The organization says the lagoon now has improved prospects for recovery compared to previous years.

cards.headline: Vero Beach Airport Offering Flights Starting at $41 in July
cards.teaser: Discount fares from Vero Beach Regional Airport begin next month.
cards.body:
Vero Beach Regional Airport will offer flights starting at $41 in July. The low-cost fares represent some of the cheapest air travel options available from the Vero Beach facility.

The $41 tickets are the starting price point for July departures from VRB. The airport serves as a regional option for travelers in Indian River County seeking alternatives to larger Florida airports.

The discount flights are now available for booking. Travelers can purchase the July fares through standard airline booking channels.

cards.headline: North Indian River County Restaurants Announce Weekly Specials
cards.teaser: Multiple restaurants in the northern part of Indian River County have rolled out new weekly deals.
cards.body:
Restaurants in north Indian River County and south Brevard County are offering weekly specials. Sebastian Daily reported the promotional offers cover multiple dining establishments in the area.

The weekly specials include discounted menu items and special pricing at participating restaurants. The promotions are designed to attract weekday and weekend diners to local establishments.

The restaurant deals are ongoing on a weekly basis. Diners can check with individual restaurants for specific offerings and schedules.

cards.headline: Two Indian River County Restaurants Earn Perfect Health Inspection Scores
cards.teaser: A pair of local restaurants received top marks from health inspectors.
cards.body:
Two restaurants in Indian River County received perfect scores on recent health inspections. The establishments passed all inspection criteria without any violations.

The perfect scores reflect compliance with Florida food safety and sanitation regulations. Health inspectors found no deficiencies during their visits to the two dining establishments.

The restaurants are now operating with clean inspection records. The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation conducts regular inspections of food service facilities across Indian River County.

cards.headline: Retirement Planning Article Focuses on Vero Beach as Destination
cards.teaser: A financial planning article examines retiring in Vero Beach on $900,000 in savings.
cards.body:
AOL published an article analyzing retirement scenarios for Vero Beach residents. The piece examines how a 62-year-old retiree could manage living in Vero Beach with $900,000 in retirement savings.

The article positions Vero Beach as a retirement destination for those with substantial savings. The financial analysis looks at cost of living and budget management in the Indian River County city.

Vero Beach continues to attract retirees from other parts of the country. The city's coastal location and lifestyle amenities make it a frequent subject of retirement planning articles.
